source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately reporting failed municipal water-quality tests to protect the public

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
Identify the test parameter(s) that failed to meet the regulatory standards.
3. Document the date and time of the failed tests.
4. Record the exact readings or measurements that resulted in the failure.
5. Note the specific test method used and any deviations from the standard protocol.
6. Identify the location or sampling point where the test was conducted within the municipal water system.
7. Prepare a report with all the gathered information.
8. Verify the accuracy and completeness of the data before finalizing the report.
9. Ensure that the information is conveyed in a clear and concise manner.
10. Include any potential health risks associated with the failed water quality parameters.
11. Report the findings to the appropriate municipal authorities responsible for water quality monitoring (e.g., the water department, public health department, etc.), according to the local regulations and procedures.
12. Communicate the findings to the public as required by local regulations and in a timely manner to ensure public safety
